headline: Committee discussed Greeley Park's history, ownership, and plans for a future Master Plan; no formal votes taken.
summary: The Greeley Park Advisory Committee reviewed the park's historical background, including unconfirmed claims about its designer and details about the original land grant. Members discussed ways to inform the public, requested maps and funding information for a Master Plan, and assigned follow-up tasks including contacting city staff for deeds, mission statement copies, and DPW plans.
plain_text:
Greeley Park Advisory Committee 
Mines Fall Conference Room 
848 West Hollis Street 
 
 
Date: September 9, 2026 
Call to Order: 5:00 PM 
 
Attendees:  
Committee Members: Stephanie Ballentine, Vicki Donchess, Kathy Lodi, Alison Galipeau, Kerry 
Miller   
DPW Assistant Director: Matt LeBlanc  
City Planner: Matthew Sullivan 
Alderman: Trish Klee 
Nashua Conservation Commission: Dick Widhu  
Quorum was determined to be present 
Approval of Minutes: The minutes of the August meeting were not available, nor approved, as they 
were not found on website by members. Trish Klee and Matt LeBlanc confirmed. Last meeting, salient 
points were reviewed. Will follow up with Claire Edwards re posting the Minutes 
Public Comment: no public attendees or comment 
Discussion and Follow Up: 
Kathy Lodi continues to review the Historical Context of the Park.  She has not been able to find any 
evidence that the Park was designed by Frederick Law Olmsted. Will continue to look for more details in 
old records. Potential contacts include Dan Hudson and Mark Sanders in the Engineering department, 
the Planning Department, Public Works, and the historical society. 
Noted the Park's land was willed to the city with the stipulation that it must be kept as open public space, 
and no for-profit businesses can be established on the grounds. Evidence that initially, 160 acres were 
deeded, buy various amounts and been added and removed, shrinking the total acreage that is counted 
today. 
Ways to disseminate info to the interested public was revisited – consider the E-Newspapers, Library 
postings, City Hall Website - Parks and Recreation webpage and the DPW Facebook page. 
Matt Sullivan will share maps of Greeley, as “portioned out” into different areas so members can start 
discussion of Master Planning for each area of the Park. Dick Widhu suggests some reference and public 
awareness plan be made to the Abenaki peoples. These Native Americans inhabited the Nashua area 
prior to the European settlements.
Matt Sullivan discussed request for Proposal (RFP) and funding status for a Master Plan. Developing this 
Plan is a multi-year process, and it was suggested that the Committee request FY28 funds for evaluation 
and planning. There may be some existing funds available as well.  
A copy of the will is considered crucial for the Master Plan also. 
It was again emphasized that any forestry management, should be delayed until a comprehensive Master 
Plan is developed.  
Playground Repairs: Discussion deferred 
Request for Short- and Long-range Plans for repairs, changes, and updates in Greeley. Matt LeBlanc 
suggests contacting Lauren Byers, Communications Administrator, Div of Public Works for this –    
To Do Items: 
• Obtain copies (from Lauren Byer) of agenda for DPW plans for changes and improvements, 
repairs of the Park; near-future as well as long-range.  
• Obtain copies of GPAC Mission Statement – Nashua City Ordinance O-22-015 
• Next BPW meeting Sept 24 at 4PM, in the Conf Room of the DPW. K Lodi and F Murphy will speak 
to the Board. 
• M Sullivan will send Greeley Park “areas” map to Claire to distribute to Members. We will discuss 
the first 3 areas at the next meeting. He will also bring copies of Deed and Will to next meeting 
(there are multiple Deeds). 
• Need Copies of the GP Advisory Committee Mission Statement 
• Ask Dean Shaloup re Olmstead Firm Park design? Master Plan (who is doing this?) 
 
Adjourned: 6:30PM 
 
Submitted September 14, 2026 
Stephanie Ballentine
